newsitem.title: USA: Shipments of blood test strips halted on FDA inquiry.
newsitem.headline: Shipments of blood test strips halted on FDA inquiry.

text.p: Shipments of paper test strips used by diabetics to monitor their blood sugar levels were halted by the manufacturer after the Food and Drug Administration questioned the strips' reliability.
Diagnostic Solutions Inc., of Irvine, Calif., stopped shipping its Quik Check strips in December, a spokesman for Chronimed Inc., which distributes the strips, said Wednesday.
Chronimed's stock price fell $2.75 to $12.25 per share Wednesday on concern that the company's profits could be hurt by the strip supply problem.

"Diagnostic Solutions is working with (the FDA) actively to reach resolution, but we have gotten no signal ... as to when that would occur," said Norman Cocke, chief financial officer at Minneapolis-based Chronimed.

Diabetics must check their blood glucose levels several times daily. Most do so by pricking a finger and dabbing the drop of blood onto a paper strip that is inserted into a machine that tests it for glucose level. Both the strips and machines are sold in drugstores.
Quik Check strips are designed to be used with the popular OneTouch blood glucose monitor manufactured by Johnson & Johnson, the New Jersey-based healthcare products giant.
Quik Check strips are the only generic option to J&J's branded OneTouch strips and sell for about 20 percent less.
The FDA is investigating Diagnostic Solutions, said an FDA spokeswoman who declined further comment.
Independent tests and in-house tests done by Chronimed show Quik Check strips meet industry standards and render consistently reliable blood test results, Cocke said.
Privately held Diagnostic Solutions could not be reached for comment.
